draft_context.source_title: Sonos Beam Ultra review: one of the best compact Dolby Atmos soundbars around
draft_context.description: Sonos Beam Ultra review The Sonos Beam Ultra doesn’t merely feel like an evolution of the pre-existing Beam products. Instead, it feels like something of a middle child between the Sonos Beam Gen 2 and the Sonos Arc Ultra. After all, it sits bang in between its sibling models when it comes to channel configuration, boasting a 7.1.2 setup with nine drivers, and while it has up-firing drivers for true Dolby Atmos, it still maintains a fairly compact design. But the Beam Ultra certainly isn’t an awkward middle-child; it’s a highly capable mid-range option that provides striking cinematic sound, while still being able to fit into a smaller setup. But is the Sonos Beam Ultra worth its $699 / £699 / AU$1,099 asking price? Like most of the best soundbars , the Sonos Beam Ultra supports Dolby Atmos (though notably Sonos omits DTS:X), and it handles the format very effectively. When watching a 4K UHD Blu-ray of The Mask , the soundbar seamlessly tracked the titular character as he tornadoes across the screen, with audio sounding as if it far exceeded the limited confines of the soundbar. When The Mask jumped upwards, diagonally, his upward trajectory was captured with precision. (Image credit: Future) And the Beam Ultra continued to impress me with its height effects across multiple movies. For instance, in Godzilla Minus One , the sense of a plane flying overhead was replicated more naturally than I expected from a mid-range bar. When Godzilla first appeared, the width of the kaiju’s movement was handled brilliantly — it sounded as if the creature’s stomping and destruction were emanating from different corners of the testing room, rather than a set of speakers, even without the help of surround speakers. What’s more, the Sonos Beam Ultra nails the fundamentals. Watching Top Gun: Maverick , the roar of jet engines was palpable, and I found this to be the case across multiple films. For a mid-sized standalone bar, the Beam Ultra produces incredibly regimented, deep, and responsive low-end sound, which is excellent for movies with high-octane action sequences and dark, impactful scores. The Beam Ultra can also get seriously loud if you want to fill a more open space, but I never noticed any tinniness or harsh compression. Still, this doesn’t come at the expense of sounds elsewhere in the frequency range. I found dialogue to be generally clear and detailed too, though I will note that turning on the Speech Enhancement mode and setting it to Medium gave me the best results. This means you can bring voices forward without hampering the fidelity of other elements in the mix. The Beam Ultra even proved to be a hit for music, whether I was listening to an Atmos or stereo mix. With an Atmos mix of I’m Gonna Love You Just A Little More Baby by Barry White, there was tremendous width to the guitars, the vocals were perfectly clear in the center, and the bass had pleasant warmth to it. Moving over to First Summer by H.K., deep bass came through with attention-grabbing impact, sounding more full-sounding than I’d anticipated, yet keys and vocal chops in the mid-range still maintained excellent clarity, as did articulate drums in the treble. (Image credit: Future) The Sonos Beam Ultra isn’t just a great performer; it’s also rammed full of useful features. TruePlay is here, which can optimize sound for your room in mere seconds, but there are also ways to manually adapt audio. For instance, you can adjust height effects to your choosing, and there’s even a height-effect simulation mode if there’s less than four inches of space above your soundbar — ideal if you’re placing the Beam Ultra on a shelf in your TV stand, say. I've already mentioned the Speech Enhancement mode, which has multiple levels to emphasize speech as little or much as you need, but there’s also a Night mode if you don’t want to disturb others. You can turn these options on in the Sonos app, but there’s also an option to add a voice assistant if you want to make adjustments on the fly. The Beam Ultra can, as you'd expect, also interact with other components in your Sonos system. You can pair compatible speakers, such as the Sonos Play , and use them as surround speakers. TV Audio Swap is also back, and enables you to transfer sound from your Beam Ultra to your Sonos Ace or Sonos Ace Ultra headphones. I tried this out with the latter cans, and found that switching was speedy and responsive, while the quality of spatial audio was exceptional — make sure to read my Sonos Ace Ultra review for a deeper dive. There are a fair few ways to connect to your Sonos Beam Ultra too. Of course, HDMI eARC is the most important — this is what you’ll use to hook the soundbar up to your TV and experience Dolby Atmos movies in all their glory. There’s also Wi-Fi 6 for streaming content over a local connection, allowing you to use services like Tidal Connect and Spotify Connect. And, unlike with the Beam Gen 2, you also get Bluetooth 5.3 connectivity as well as USB-C line-in. One thing I would have really have loved to see, though, is an HDMI input, which has been left off of the Sonos Beam Ultra. Given that connecting the soundbar up to your TV already takes away one precious HDMI slot, it would’ve been great to get a passthrough port on this model — it’s something I use on my Marshall Heston 120 at home, given that I have multiple game consoles connected up. Something that does not disappoint, though, is the Beam Ultra’s design. It’s sleek, modern, and stylish — but understated enough to seamlessly slot into just about any living space. It also has a great standard of build, intuitive touch controls, and handy status indicator lights to signify connection status. There’s also a microphone slider, which you can deactivate if you don’t want your soundbar listening in on you. But here comes the big question: is the Sonos Beam Ultra actually worth the money? While $699 / £699 / AU$1,099 is by no means cheap, I still think the answer is yes. It’s priced right in between the Beam Gen 2 and Arc Ultra, and feels like a true best-of-both-worlds option — the height channels give it much more convincing Atmos performance than the Beam Gen 2, but you also get amazing power in a single, compact package. Sure, you could get a soundbar and sub combo like the Samsung HW-Q800F for a similar price, and that will give you even deeper, more cinematic bass. But that model has a more restrictive 5.1.2 configuration, and if you want something more low-profile, it won’t fit the bill. You also get an excellent suite of features from the Beam Ultra, and you can add a compatible sub and other other Sonos speakers for surround sound if you wish. As a result, the Sonos Beam Ultra might just be the best compact Dolby Atmos soundbar I’ve tested. In spite of its modest size, it plates up powerful, immersive, and clear audio, so if you want a simple plug-and-play solution to get amazing audio into just about any space, this is my top recommendation. (Image credit: Future) Sonos Beam Ultra review: Price and release date Priced at $699 / £699 / AU$1,099 Released in September 2026 The Sonos Beam Ultra is priced at $699 / £699 / AU$1,099, placing it mid-way between the Sonos Beam Gen 2 and the Sonos Arc Ultra. While you can get some multi-box options for a similar price, like the Sony HW-Q800F, for instance, the Beam Ultra features an extensive 7.1.2 driver configuration, and its compact nature is a central part of its appeal. Sonos Beam Ultra review: specs Dimensions 29.5 x 2.6 x 4.1 inches / 750 x 65 x 105mm Speaker channels 7.1.2 Connections HDMI eARC, Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5.3, USB-C Dolby Atmos / DTS:X Yes / No Sub included No Rear speakers included No (Image credit: Future) Should I buy the Sonos Beam Ultra? Attribute Notes Score Features Good connectivity options, great sound modes, can add sub and surrounds, no DTS:X or HDMI passthrough. 4.5/5 Performance Expansive sound in a compact package with imposing bass and clear dialogue. 5/5 Design Stellar looks, slim build, neat touch controls. 5/5 Setup & usability Plug and play set-up, easy to connect to via Wi-Fi or Bluetooth. 5/5 Value Not cheap, but a perfect marriage of the standard Beam and Arc that’s priced accordingly. 4.5/5 Buy it if… You want a compact soundbar with amazing Dolby Atmos So many compact Dolby Atmos soundbars fall flat when it comes to Dolby Atmos. Often, that’s due to a lack of dedicated up-firing drivers to provide convincing height effects. But the Beam Ultra has those — and it also conjures up an impressive sense of width. You already own a Sonos system If you already have a compatible sub and speakers like the Sonos Play or Sonos Era 100 , you can connect them to the Beam Ultra to open up even more immersive, three-dimensional audio. TV Audio Swap is also available if you’ve got the Sonos Ace or Sonos Ace Ultra headphones. Don’t buy it if… You need HDMI passthrough The Sonos Beam Ultra does not offer HDMI passthrough, which might be troublesome if, like me, you have multiple games consoles, a 4K Blu-ray player, and other devices that use HDMI. You need DTS:X The Sonos Beam Ultra supports Dolby Atmos, but not DTS:X, much like other Sonos soundbars, including the Sonos Arc Ultra. A number of 4K discs make use of DTS:X, so if you’re someone who often makes use of that format, it may be worth looking elsewhere. Sonos Beam Ultra review: also consider Sonos Beam Ultra Samsung HW-Q800F Bose Smart Ultra Soundbar Price $699 / £699 / AU$1,099 $1,099 / £799 / AU$1,099 £899 / $899 / AU$1499 Dimensions 29.5 x 2.6 x 4.1 inches / 750 x 65 x 105mm Main soundbar: 43.7 x 2.4 x 4.7 inches / 1110.7 x 60.4 x 120mm; subwoofer: 9.8 x 9.9 x 9.8 inches / 249 x 251.8 x 249mm 2.3 x 41 x 4.2 inches / 58 x 1045 x 107mm Speaker channels 7.1.2 5.1.2 5.1.2 Connections HDMI eARC, Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5.3, USB-C 1x HDMI input, 1x HDMI eARC, digital optical, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth 5.3 HDMI eARC, digital optical, Ethernet, USB (service only), Bluetooth, Wi-Fi Dolby Atmos / DTS:X Yes / No Yes / Yes Yes / No Sub included No Yes No Rear speakers included No No No Samsung HW-Q800F This multi-box Samsung soundbar can now be found for a similar price to the Sonos Beam Ultra, if not less. It supplies exceptional sound, with impeccable bass from its dedicated sub, clear dialogue, and engrossing Atmos effects. It doesn’t offer the Beam Ultra’s compact size, but it does have DTS:X and HDMI passthrough. Read my full Samsung HW-Q800F review . Bose Smart Ultra Soundbar The Bose Smart Ultra Soundbar is a great 5.1.2 soundbar with wide, detailed sound, excellent build quality, and an effective companion app. It doesn’t quite offer the height or bass weight of the Sonos Beam Ultra, but it can often be found on sale for less than $700 / £500. Read our full Bose Smart Ultra Soundbar review . How I tested the Sonos Beam Ultra (Image credit: Future) I spent one week testing the soundbar in our TV testing space at Future Labs I watched a variety of movies, and listened to music in both Dolby Atmos and stereo formats I spent one week testing the Sonos Beam Ultra at our TV testing space at Future Labs, during which time I exhausted its various features, watched a variety of movies, and listened to music in both Dolby Atmos and stereo formats. To test the Beam Ultra, I hooked it up to the Samsung R95H TV via HDMI. I also made use of the Panasonic DP-UB820 to view Dolby Atmos-enabled 4K UHD Blu-rays. When listening to music, I streamed tunes over Tidal Connect via Wi-Fi, and made use of the TV Audio Swap feature to transfer audio from the soundbar to the Sonos Ace Ultra headphones. I also compared the Sonos Beam Ultra directly against the Sonos Beam Gen 2 to assess improvements to height effects, expansiveness, and general functionality. I’ve spent several years testing audio-visual gear at TechRadar, where I'm a Senior Reviews Writer. I’ve tested a vast number of soundbars specifically, from compact models like the Marshall Heston 60 to grand surround systems like the LG Sound Suite Immersive Suite 7 Pro . How much RAM will I need in my laptop? You’ll want at least 8GB, though 16GB is preferable, especially if you play games. Don’t buy laptops with under 4GB of RAM or 128GB of SSD storage—though on a Chromebook or a budget Windows machine, this configuration is acceptable. Check out our article on how much RAM does a laptop need for more in-depth info. 2. What’s the difference between a Chromebook and a Windows laptop? The one big difference between a Chromebook and a Windows laptop is the operating system. Chromebooks run ChromeOS and Windows run, well, Microsoft Windows. Chromebooks make good everyday machines because they’re designed for browsing the web, checking e-mail, and so on. They use less resources and are generally more affordable than the Windows variety. They also don’t need antivirus protection. A Windows laptop is a lot more versatile in what it can do, and not just in terms of running local programs. You can really pump a Windows laptop up with a ton of RAM, storage, and so on. 3. When should I look for a laptop deal? You’ll likely find the best laptop deals during Prime Day (mid-July), Black Friday (the day after Thanksgiving), and back-to-school season (June-August). Sure, you’ll find good laptop deals throughout the year, but if you really want to save big, we’d recommend scoping out your favorite online retailers during those times. 4. Which retailers offer the best deals? You can find all kinds of deals across a wide range of online retailers such as Newegg , Walmart , Best Buy , Amazon , and so on. However, we’d recommend checking out deals from laptop manufacturers like Lenovo , HP , and Dell . You’ll usually find many different configurations on sale and the discounts can be pretty darn steep. For more options, check out PCWorld’s roundup of the best laptops available right now.

The gorgeous 16-inch 2880×1800 OLED display also offers vibrant colors and crisp detail, so everything from Excel spreadsheets to Netflix shows should look fantastic.

articles.title: Meta patches Muse exploit that let attackers control the AI agent
articles.hook: Meta has issued a patch for its Muse macOS app following the discovery of a zero-day vulnerability that could allow someone to take control of the AI agent.
articles.summary: Meta has issued a patch for its Muse macOS app following the discovery of a zero-day vulnerability that could allow someone to take control of the AI agent. The bug found by security researcher Patrick Wardle utilized an undocumented Muse setting that enabled potential attackers running local code to redirect transcription processing from Meta’s servers to their own endpoint, Ars Technica reports, giving the attacker access to the Muse account.
articles.dek: Meta has issued a patch for its Muse macOS app following the discovery of a zero-day vulnerability that could allow someone to take control of the AI agent.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.body: The bug found by security researcher Patrick Wardle utilized an undocumented Muse setting that enabled potential attackers running local code to redirect transcription processing from Meta’s servers to their own endpoint, Ars Technica reports, giving the attacker access to the Muse account.

sections.heading: Where the sources line up
sections.body: Several design decisions reportedly enabled this flaw, including having Muse dictation occur in the cloud instead of on-device, and allowing any app to control all of Muse’s undocumented settings. Proof-of-concept attacks developed by Wardle to test the exploit enabled him to take pictures and write malicious files to disk via Muse, which did not alert the user in many cases.

sections.heading: Practical impact for readers
sections.body: “This was a local privilege escalation attack, not a remote exploit. Using it to do harm therefore requires malicious code already running on the user’s machine under their user account and the practical risk to users of the Muse Mac app was therefore quite low,” David Singleton of Meta Superintelligence Labs said on X . “Nonetheless, we have issued a hotfix to the app to address the issue.

sections.heading: Who should pay attention now
sections.body: While quickly addressed, the Muse exploit comes at a time when Meta’s AI agent is already being scrutinized as the company tries to claw back ground from rival AI providers. Amazon recently blocked Muse from accessing its e-commerce platform and claims Meta never obtained its permission to do so. Still, the launch has been successful for Meta — during its first 12 days, estimated downloads of the Muse mobile app have reportedly outpaced ChatGPT’s own 12-day debut in the US and Canada, with Meta stock climbing by 11 percent on Monday.

Pr … Read the full story at The Verge. ]]>
paragraphs: Meta has issued a patch for its Muse macOS app following the discovery of a zero-day vulnerability that could allow someone to take control of the AI agent. The bug found by security researcher Patrick Wardle utilized an undocumented Muse setting that enabled potential attackers running local code to redirect transcription processing from Meta’s servers to their own endpoint, Ars Technica reports, giving the attacker access to the Muse account.

Several design decisions reportedly enabled this flaw, including having Muse dictation occur in the cloud instead of on-device, and allowing any app to control all of Muse’s undocumented settings. Proof-of-concept attacks developed by Wardle to test the exploit enabled him to take pictures and write malicious files to disk via Muse, which did not alert the user in many cases.

“This was a local privilege escalation attack, not a remote exploit. Using it to do harm therefore requires malicious code already running on the user’s machine under their user account and the practical risk to users of the Muse Mac app was therefore quite low,” David Singleton of Meta Superintelligence Labs said on X . “Nonetheless, we have issued a hotfix to the app to address the issue.”

While quickly addressed, the Muse exploit comes at a time when Meta’s AI agent is already being scrutinized as the company tries to claw back ground from rival AI providers. Amazon recently blocked Muse from accessing its e-commerce platform and claims Meta never obtained its permission to do so. Still, the launch has been successful for Meta — during its first 12 days, estimated downloads of the Muse mobile app have reportedly outpaced ChatGPT’s own 12-day debut in the US and Canada, with Meta stock climbing by 11 percent on Monday.

articles.title: Mở hộp Mac mini dùng chip M6 giá từ 25 triệu đồng
articles.hook: Với sự xuất hiện của MacBook Neo, Mac mini không còn là máy tính Mac rẻ nhất của Apple như khi mới nâng cấp chip M4 năm 2024.
articles.summary: Với sự xuất hiện của MacBook Neo, Mac mini không còn là máy tính Mac rẻ nhất của Apple như khi mới nâng cấp chip M4 năm 2024. So với hai năm trước, giá khởi điểm của máy cũng tăng khoảng 10 triệu, từ 14,9 triệu lên 24,9 triệu đồng cho lựa chọn RAM 16 GB, SSD 256 GB.
articles.dek: Với sự xuất hiện của MacBook Neo, Mac mini không còn là máy tính Mac rẻ nhất của Apple như khi mới nâng cấp chip M4 năm 2024.

sections.heading: Điều gì đã xảy ra
sections.body: So với hai năm trước, giá khởi điểm của máy cũng tăng khoảng 10 triệu, từ 14,9 triệu lên 24,9 triệu đồng cho lựa chọn RAM 16 GB, SSD 256 GB. Tuy nhiên, việc tăng giá hiện là "bình thường mới" của thị trường máy tính khi chỉ tính riêng bộ nhớ RAM cùng dung lượng, giá mua lẻ đã tăng 3-4 lần trong hai năm qua.

sections.heading: Các nguồn đang khớp nhau ở đâu
sections.body: Điểm sáng là Apple vẫn có thể cung cấp đầy đủ lựa chọn RAM, SSD cho người dùng, tối đa 64 GB và 8 TB tương ứng trong khi hầu hết nhà sản xuất máy tính phải cắt bỏ tùy chọn cao cấp. Điều này cho thấy việc làm chủ chuỗi cung ứng vẫn khiến hãng tạo sự khác biệt cho người dùng cao cấp của Mac mini, Mac Studio nói riêng và các dòng máy tính Mac nói chung.

sections.heading: Dữ kiện hiện có
sections.body: Mac mini 2026 ra mắt ngày 25/8, là lần đầu Apple giới thiệu máy tính Mac mới ngay trước thềm sự kiện quan trọng nhất đầu tháng 9 với tâm điểm iPhone thế hệ mới. Các phiên bản trước đó đều xuất hiện vào tháng 10 hoặc nửa đầu năm với dòng MacBook. Mac mini lần này ra mắt cùng Mac Studio và hai vi xử lý mới là M6 và M5 Ultra.

sections.heading: Ai nên chú ý lúc này
sections.body: Trong ảnh là phiên bản cấu hình khởi điểm với RAM 16 GB, SSD 256 GB, chip M6 có giá 24,9 triệu, hoặc 22,219 triệu đồng cho học sinh, sinh viên, người làm việc trong ngành giáo dục.

sections.heading: Điều chưa rõ
sections.body: Mac mini M6 không thay đổi thiết kế với cách bố trí phím nguồn ở mặt đáy vốn gây tranh cãi từ thế hệ trước. Khi muốn mở, người dùng phải lật lên và xoay ra phía trước để bấm khá bất tiện. Trong khi đó, Mac Studio cũng có vỏ nhôm nguyên khối nhưng có nút nguồn ở vị trí thuận tiện hơn.

draft_context.source_title: Mở hộp Mac mini dùng chip M6 giá từ 25 triệu đồng
draft_context.description: Mac mini 2026 sử dụng chip 2 nm đầu tiên của Apple là M6, nhưng giá khởi điểm cao hơn phiên bản M4 ra mắt hai năm trước do khủng hoảng chip nhớ toàn cầu.
paragraphs: Với sự xuất hiện của MacBook Neo, Mac mini không còn là máy tính Mac rẻ nhất của Apple như khi mới nâng cấp chip M4 năm 2024. So với hai năm trước, giá khởi điểm của máy cũng tăng khoảng 10 triệu, từ 14,9 triệu lên 24,9 triệu đồng cho lựa chọn RAM 16 GB, SSD 256 GB. Tuy nhiên, việc tăng giá hiện là "bình thường mới" của thị trường máy tính khi chỉ tính riêng bộ nhớ RAM cùng dung lượng, giá mua lẻ đã tăng 3-4 lần trong hai năm qua.

Điểm sáng là Apple vẫn có thể cung cấp đầy đủ lựa chọn RAM, SSD cho người dùng, tối đa 64 GB và 8 TB tương ứng trong khi hầu hết nhà sản xuất máy tính phải cắt bỏ tùy chọn cao cấp. Điều này cho thấy việc làm chủ chuỗi cung ứng vẫn khiến hãng tạo sự khác biệt cho người dùng cao cấp của Mac mini, Mac Studio nói riêng và các dòng máy tính Mac nói chung.

Mac mini 2026 ra mắt ngày 25/8, là lần đầu Apple giới thiệu máy tính Mac mới ngay trước thềm sự kiện quan trọng nhất đầu tháng 9 với tâm điểm iPhone thế hệ mới. Các phiên bản trước đó đều xuất hiện vào tháng 10 hoặc nửa đầu năm với dòng MacBook. Mac mini lần này ra mắt cùng Mac Studio và hai vi xử lý mới là M6 và M5 Ultra.
Trong ảnh là phiên bản cấu hình khởi điểm với RAM 16 GB, SSD 256 GB, chip M6 có giá 24,9 triệu, hoặc 22,219 triệu đồng cho học sinh, sinh viên, người làm việc trong ngành giáo dục.

Mac mini M6 không thay đổi thiết kế với cách bố trí phím nguồn ở mặt đáy vốn gây tranh cãi từ thế hệ trước. Khi muốn mở, người dùng phải lật lên và xoay ra phía trước để bấm khá bất tiện. Trong khi đó, Mac Studio cũng có vỏ nhôm nguyên khối nhưng có nút nguồn ở vị trí thuận tiện hơn.

Thói quen sử dụng thực tế có thể khác với mỗi người nhưng với macOS, người dùng thường ít tắt máy hơn so với máy tính Windows, chỉ khóa máy và vào chế độ ngủ, khi cần sử dụng sẽ nhấn bàn phím, chuột để mở lại.

articles.title: Mẹ của Elon Musk ngủ trong gara khi đến thăm con
articles.hook: "Đó là ngôi nhà nhỏ với một chiếc giường nhỏ trong gara", bà Maye Musk nói với Fox Business cuối tuần qua về nơi ở của Musk tại Texas.
articles.summary: "Đó là ngôi nhà nhỏ với một chiếc giường nhỏ trong gara", bà Maye Musk nói với Fox Business cuối tuần qua về nơi ở của Musk tại Texas. Bà Maye cho biết có thể di chuyển khoảng 45 phút đến khách sạn nhưng vẫn chọn nghỉ trong gara, thêm rằng đã có "truyền thống gia đình" như vậy. "Khi mẹ tôi chuyển từ Nam Phi về Canada, bà ngủ trong gara. Còn khi các con tôi đi học đại học, tôi ngủ trên sàn nhà hoặc trên ghế sofa sau khi dọn hết mấy hộp pizza", bà tiếp tục.
Bà Maye Musk đăng ảnh bên các con trong dịp Lễ quốc khánh Mỹ 4/7, từ trái qua: Tosca, Elon, Maye và Kimbal. Ảnh: Instagram/Maye Musk
Là người mẫu, chuyên gia dinh dưỡng và diễn giả nổi tiếng, bà Maye cho biết bà thường tận hưởng những nơi nghỉ ngơi sang trọng, nhưng con trai lại luôn thích ở nơi gần công việc nhất có thể.

Elon Musk nhiều lần chia sẻ ông có thể nghỉ ngơi ở nơi nào thuận tiện. "Có thời gian tôi ngủ dưới gầm bàn làm việc", tỷ phú Mỹ nói tại Hội nghị Đầu tư Baron năm 2022 khi nhắc đến giai đoạn xây nhà máy Tesla năm 2010. "Ngủ trên sàn nhà thật sự khó chịu. Và mỗi khi thức dậy, tôi đều ngửi thấy mùi bụi kim loại".

draft_context.description: At Mozilla, we consider security to be a paramount aspect of the web. This is why not only does Firefox have a long running bug bounty program but also mature release management and security engineering practices. These practices combined with well-trained and talented Firefox teams are also the reason why we respond to security bugs as quickly as we do. This week at the security hacking competition pwn2own, security researchers demonstrated two new content-process exploits against Firefox. Neither of the attacks managed to break out of our sandbox, which is required to gain control over the user’s system. Out of abundance of caution, we just released new Firefox versions in response to these attacks – all within the same day of the second exploit announcement. The updated versions are Firefox 138.0.4, Firefox ESR 128.10.1, Firefox ESR 115.23.1 and Firefox for Android. Despite the limited impact of these attacks, all users and administrators are advised to update Firefox as soon as possible. Just last year at the same security event, we responded to an exploitable security bug within 21 hours , for which we earned an award as the fastest to patch . But this year was special. This year, two security researchers signed up to attack Firefox at pwn2own. We continued the same rapid security response this year too. Background Pwn2Own is an annual computer hacking contest where participants aim to find security vulnerabilities in major software such as browsers. This year, the event was held in Berlin, Germany, and a lot of popular software was listed as potential targets for security research . As part of the event preparation, we were informed that Firefox was also listed as a target. But it took until the day before the event when we learned that not just one but two groups signed up to demonstrate their work. Typically, people attacking a browser require a multi-step exploit. At first, they need to compromise the web browser tab to gain limited control of the user’s system. But due to Firefox’s robust security architecture, another bug (a sandbox escape) is required to break out of the current tab and gain wider system access. Unlike prior years, neither participating group was able to escape our sandbox this year. We have verbal confirmation that this is attributed to the recent architectural improvements to our Firefox sandbox which have neutered a wide range of such attacks. This continues to build confidence in Firefox’s strong security posture. To review and fix the reported exploits a diverse team of people from all across the world and in various roles (engineering, QA, release management, security and many more) rushed to work. We tested and released a new version of Firefox for all of our supported platforms, operating systems, and configurations with rapid speed. Our work does not end here. We continue to use opportunities like this to improve our incident response. We will also continue to study the reports to identify new hardening features and security improvements to keep all of our Firefox users across the globe protected. Related Resources If you’re interested in learning more about Mozilla’s security initiatives or Firefox security, here are some resources to help you get started: Mozilla Security Mozilla Security Blog Bug Bounty Program Furthermore, if you want to kickstart your own security research in Firefox, we invite you to follow our deeply technical blog at Attack & Defense – Firefox Security Internals for Engineers, Researchers, and Bounty Hunters . Update – August 7th, 2025 We are pleased to share that Mozilla was awarded the Vanguard “Speedrunner” Award by the Zero Day Initiative (ZDI). This is in regonition to being consistently fast throghout the last 20 years of Zero Day Initiative’s pwn2own events. “Speedrunner” trophy, awarded to Mozilla Firefox for an outstanding security response during pwn2own. The post Firefox Security Response to pwn2own 2025 appeared first on Mozilla Security Blog .
